I'm an economist at U.S. Bank, where I lead the design of the economic scenarios the bank uses to plan for downturns and set aside reserves for loan losses. Before that, I spent four years at the U.S. Treasury working on international finance, including IMF lending and the response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

I live in the Charlotte area with my wife and our twins. I grew up in Ohio and have lived in South Carolina, Wisconsin, Washington, D.C., and Minnesota along the way. When I'm not working, I'm usually out for a run or a ride, in the gym, or partway through a fantasy series, and there's a good chance a board game is on the table.

Most of my work is built in R, and lately I've been using AI tools to do more of it. This site is one result: a small set of charts on the U.S. economy that I keep current, many of them extending analyses I thought deserved a longer life.

- [Inflation](inflation.qmd): measures of consumer price inflation
